summary: Round 6 delta is two comment blocks and one tightened assertion. The code half is right and I measured it rather than accepted it: isEqualTo(26L) is the true count on that fixture (deterministic -- MemoryBinStore, frozen checkpoint and renew tickers, no background requests), the Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence() - 1, upTo) off-by-one measures 27 there, and under that mutant three tests now fail (aPredecessorTOOSHORTToCheckpointStillStopsAtItsAncestorsCheckpoint 27 vs 26, aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed 19 vs 18, aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem 15 vs 14). The full :sequencer:test suite is green in my own tree with the mutant reverted, and 17/17 for the bounded takeover (the number LocalSequencerFailoverTest's new comment quotes) measured directly. Nothing in this delta touches request behaviour; the commit's rate story still scales with epochs walked, never with records or streams. What the delta DID do is falsify its own neighbours: the merged comment describes the sibling assertion as it was BEFORE the sibling edit in the same two-file delta, and the newly added comment above that assertion says the off-by-one is killed only elsewhere, fifteen characters above the line that now kills it. That is instance six and seven of this milestone's recurring shape, and it is worth saying that both were CREATED by round 5's and round 6's fixes, not by the change. All three findings are minor and none blocks: no production behaviour, no weakened assertion, no cost claim that is wrong. review.md rule minors-land applies, and review.sh's own over-budget banner already prescribes the remedy -- delete the prose that keeps being wrong rather than correct it a seventh time.

findings.title: The merged comment describes the sibling assertion as it was before the other half of this same delta changed it -- instance six of the shape the merged comment itself is about
findings.detail: The merged sentence reads: 'Two of the sibling suite's three cost tests compare two MEASUREMENTS rather than a number, which a recovery issuing six redundant requests satisfies perfectly; the third bounds a total. This count and the burned-epoch one are the EXACT ones.' The sibling suite is LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest and it does have exactly three cost tests -- but the OTHER hunk of this same two-file delta changed the third from isLessThanOrEqualTo(30L) to isEqualTo(26L). So 'the third bounds a total' is false as of these staged bytes, and 'this count and the burned-epoch one are the EXACT ones' undercounts: there are now three exact request-count assertions on the bounded path (18, 14, 26), which is exactly what this commit's own backlog row asserts one clause later -- 'EVERY COST ASSERTION ON THE BOUNDED PATH IS NOW EXACT'. The comment and the row contradict each other inside one commit. The prescription that produced this merge was mine, and it was to merge rather than qualify; the merge itself was done correctly, but it was written against the pre-edit sibling.
findings.failure_scenario: M5's fallback ladder (or any later change that moves a constant on this path) reopens these counts. The maintainer reads the correctness suite -- which is where this commit put the authoritative statement of which counts are exact and why -- learns that the sibling's third cost test merely 'bounds a total' and that only two counts in the tree are exact, and re-relaxes isEqualTo(26L) to an inequality on the strength of that description. The same file records, in the comment directly above that assertion, that an inequality there is precisely what hid a live off-by-one at 27 requests. A false inventory is what makes a forbidden relaxation look like restoring the intended form.
findings.prescription: Do not re-state the inventory a third time; DELETE the cross-file clause. The sentence only needs to say why THIS count is exact ('an inequality leaves room a regression can live in'), which is true forever and does not go stale when a neighbouring file's assertion changes. An inventory of which assertions in other files are exact is guaranteed to be falsified by the next commit that changes one -- that property, not carelessness, is what produced instances one through six. If it is left as-is instead, say so in the commit body: it is a minor and it lands.

findings.title: 'It is killed only by the exact counts in the sibling suite' is measured false by the assertion on the next line
findings.detail: The new comment says of the Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence() - 1, upTo) off-by-one: 'measures 27 and stayed green under `<= 30`. It is killed only by the exact counts in the sibling suite, which is an argument for this one being exact too, not against it.' The first clause is past tense and true. The second is present tense and false as of these bytes: I applied that exact mutant in my own copy of the staged tree and it now fails THREE tests, this one among them -- 'the walk stopped at the first ancestor that HAS a checkpoint' expected 26L but was 27L. The sentence describes the world the edit on the line below it just ended, and it sits four lines above the assertion that refutes it. Same shape as M4.9-R6-1: the correction and the claim it corrects both left standing.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer weighing whether isEqualTo(26L) is load-bearing reads its own comment saying the mutation it is supposed to catch is caught only somewhere else, concludes this count is redundant coverage carried for tidiness, and relaxes or deletes it when the constant next moves. It is the only assertion in the tree that constrains cost on the too-short-predecessor path -- the path the file's own comment calls 'the common one' -- so losing it returns that path to an unpinned budget while the two sibling equality tests stay green, because they compare two measurements and a constant overhead cancels.
findings.prescription: One word: 'It WAS killed only by the exact counts in the sibling suite -- and now here too, at 27 against 26.' Or drop the clause entirely and keep 'an inequality leaves room a regression can live in', which is the part that stays true.

findings.title: BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest's class javadoc says every assertion in it asserts offsets; two of them assert request counts, one named fifteen lines below by the comment this round edited
findings.detail: The class javadoc states the suite split: 'LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest asserts request counts, and every assertion here asserts offsets.' That is false in the staged bytes -- aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed asserts counting.counts().total() isEqualTo(18L) and aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem asserts isEqualTo(14L). Both are request counts, and the merged comment this round rewrote refers to them as such ('This count and the burned-epoch one'), so the file contradicts its own header. This was falsified by an earlier round's fix, not by this one: the burned-epoch test was converted from a sentinel offset to a request count precisely because the sentinel proved the wrong thing. The first test's inline comment carries a second stale locator from the same split -- 'THE COST TESTS ABOVE ARE SATISFIED BY A RECOVERY THAT READS NOTHING AND IS WRONG' -- when there are no cost tests above it in this file any more; they are in the sibling file.
findings.failure_scenario: The suite split is the seam this commit created and the javadoc is what a maintainer reads to know where a new assertion belongs. Believing this file is offsets-only, the next person adding a bounded-path cost assertion puts it in the sibling suite, or -- worse -- deletes the 18L and 14L counts here as belonging to the other half, taking with them the only assertion that discriminates 'used the checkpoint and stopped' from 'folded the checkpoint in and walked to the origin', which this commit records as a mutant that Math::max makes invisible to every offset assertion.
findings.prescription: State the seam by what each file is FOR rather than by what every assertion in it does: this suite exists to pin what the bound reconstructs, and it counts requests where a count is the only thing that separates two behaviours with identical offsets. Fix the 'above' locator in the same edit or delete the clause.
